title: Cold rebuild: parse traceparent
summary: Rebuild the strict traceparent parser from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: You wrote **Parse traceparent like a receiver must** in *Context propagation*. Write it again from an **empty editor**.
Why this one? Broken traces are the most common tracing bug in production, and nearly all of them come down to a context that was
not passed, or a header that was mangled on the way (a proxy that upper-cases it, a queue that drops it). Knowing the format cold is
how you spot that in a packet capture or a log line.

steps.prompt: A gateway forwards `traceparent: 00-4BF92F3577B34DA6A3CE929D0E0E4736-00F067AA0BA902B7-01`. What does a strict W3C receiver do?
options: Rejects it (upper-case hex) and starts a new trace
steps.explain: The spec requires lower-case hex. The request still works; only the trace breaks in two at that hop, which is exactly how such bugs hide.

steps.title: Rebuild TryParse cold
prompt: Write `bool TryParse(string? header, out string traceId, out string parentId, out bool sampled)` again, from memory:
version `00`, exactly four parts, 32 and 16 lower-case hex digits that are not all zeros, two hex digits of flags, `sampled` = bit 0,
outer spaces trimmed, empty outputs when rejected.
